answer: Sybil resistance in an AI-agent economy rests on staked identity with slashing. An agent must post a bond of real capital before its work counts, and bad behavior can burn that bond. Forging a thousand fake peers therefore means funding a thousand stakes, not a thousand free keys. Rewards scale with verified output, not headcount, so each duplicate adds risk while expected profit stays flat. A public ledger acts as a mirror, exposing shared funding and repeated patterns early. Losses are certain as a felled timber; payouts shrink like nectar drained by crowding, so return drops below zero.
